summary:
The bullpen_fatigue category is the story to fade across every rating right now — R1/R2/R3 all sit at 41% (72-104, n=176) over the last 14 days, a full 5.1pts below season baseline, and R4's own trends and runs categories have joined the slide (trends 51% vs 57% season, runs 47% vs 52%, both COLD, with R4's runs category riding an 8-game losing streak). Runs is broadly shaky across the board — R2 is 45% at n=96 over 14 days, R1 and R3 both under .500 too — so any pick leaning heavily on runs or bullpen_fatigue signals deserves a discount today, even as SP and trends stay serviceable (R1/R2 SP at 56%, n=176). The category combos that actually hit — trends+sp at 56.9% and trends+runs at 55.8% — are your floor for trusting a play, not fatigue-driven or hitting-driven picks (hitting is 45% across R1/R2/R3 last 14 days).

On today's board, the consensus quintet up top — NYY over COL (avg delta ~+2.2), LAD over CIN (~+2.0), MIL over CHC (~+1.6), DET over MIN (~+1.3), CHW over PIT (~+1.2) — is where all four ratings stack, and MIL/BOS carry the best team-level track records when liked (MIL 62% n=55, strong 64% +9.0u; BOS 76% n=51, strong 79% +20.0u), making CHC@MIL and LAA@BOS the two strongest plays on the slate structurally, not just by delta. CHW is trending the opposite direction on volume (44% n=34, strong 50%) despite today's rating lean, so treat PIT@CHW as a smaller stake even with four-rating agreement. TOR@ATH is the lone strong fade consensus (-1.0 to -1.2 across all four boards), and with R4 still bleeding on runs (8L) and bullpen_fatigue (41%), keep size modest there. The two split games — TEX@SEA and STL@SFG — are honest coin flips where R4 diverges from the other three; skip or minimal size until lineups/SP firm up, especially with TEX@SEA still TBD on both starters.
